pr.title: Set the CI reviews' reasoning effort with project init --ci-effort
pr.head: 557fcff5099306ad9571466e9aa38b6b02f8daa7

summary: Projector can review pull requests in GitHub Actions. project init --ci-review writes the workflow .github/workflows/projector-review.yml, which runs Projector's review action once for each configured agent (Claude Code, Codex, or both). The action has always taken an effort input, the agent's reasoning effort, which defaults to high. The workflow init writes never passed that input, though, so every CI review ran at high.

Changing the effort meant editing the workflow by hand. init refreshes the workflow only while nobody has edited it, so a team that lowered the effort to save cost also stopped getting workflow updates. This pull request makes the effort a setting, the way the model already is:

• project init --ci-effort <level> records the level as review.ci_effort in .projector.toml.
  • init, and project review ci-workflow --effort, write it into the review step as effort: <level>.
  • With no level set, the workflow leaves the input out, so an existing workflow renders exactly as before and keeps the digest that marks it unedited.
  • One level applies to every agent's job. Claude Code and Codex accept different levels, so init refuses a level that any listed agent does not accept.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Effort: the agent's reasoning effort, which trades cost against how closely it reads the change.
  • Digest: the SHA-256 line at the top of the generated workflow. init replaces a workflow whose digest still matches and keeps one somebody edited.
  • Refresh: a later project init that rewrites the workflow from the recorded settings.

groups.title: Rendering the effort into the workflow
groups.kicker: Validate a level against the agents and write it as the action's input
intro: ci.py builds the workflow text from a template. This group adds a table of the levels each agent's CLI accepts, a parser that checks one level against every listed agent, and an @EFFORT@ placeholder in the review step's with: block.
When no effort is given, the placeholder becomes an empty string, so the rendered workflow and its digest are byte for byte what they were before this change.

files.note: Adds EFFORTS and parse_effort, and threads an optional effort through body and workflow_text.

checks.text: EFFORTS has an entry for both names in AGENTS, the only agents parse_agents accepts, so EFFORTS[name] cannot raise KeyError. Checked by reading AGENTS.
Rendered a workflow for claude,codex=gpt-5.5 at medium: the line lands at the with: block's indentation, before app:, and only in the review job.

files.note: The review step gains the @EFFORT@ placeholder ahead of @APP@. The summary job runs no agent, so it gets none.

groups.title: The setting and the commands
groups.kicker: Where the level comes from: the flag, then review.ci_effort
intro: ci_effort resolves the level the same way ci_runs_on resolves runner labels: the command-line flag first, then the recorded review.ci_effort, then nothing, which leaves the action's default.

init_ci_review resolves the level before it writes the workflow or records any setting, so a refused level leaves the repository as it was. It records the level only when one was given and it differs from what is recorded.

files.note: Adds --ci-effort to init and --effort to project review ci-workflow, and the ci_effort helper.

checks.text: When the level comes from review.ci_effort, the refusal still says only got 'max', so someone who adds codex later sees a level they did not type. The review listed naming the setting in that message as a suggestion.

groups.title: Documentation and plan
groups.kicker: The flag, the setting, and the plan's decision
intro: docs/review-in-ci.md gains a "Set the reasoning effort" section, and docs/cli.md documents the flag, the setting's row, and the ci-workflow option. The review-in-ci plan, still in-progress, records the decision as § 12.

files.note: § 12, "The effort is a setting", records why one level applies to every agent.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Init writes, keeps, moves, and refuses the effort
intro: The new tests run init in temporary repositories. They check that the effort appears once and only in the review job, that a later init leaves the workflow unchanged, that ci-workflow prints the same text, that no effort means no line, and that max with codex is refused before anything is written.
